headline: US stocks fell sharply on Friday as worries about heavily indebted AI companies and a jump in oil prices unsettled investors.
score_reason: Broad sell-off with AI debt stress and the Nasdaq's worst week in months, reported by Reuters and matched by other outlets; no downgrade needed.
importance_line: Savers in pension and index funds feel it first through the S&P 500's expected steepest weekly loss since January, per Reuters, then banks and funds lending to AI builders, but it is unclear whether this is a short panic, since most of this year's index gain came from the AI stocks now being sold.
summary: Reuters reports that the Nasdaq fell about 2.2% on Friday and was heading for a weekly loss above 4%, with CoreWeave, an Nvidia-backed company that rents out AI computing power, down 12% and chip stocks on course for an eighth straight daily decline. Reuters links the selling to fears that heavily indebted AI infrastructure firms may not earn enough to repay their loans as borrowing costs rise, and to oil gaining more than 3% on Middle East supply worries.
notes: Reuters wire text read on the Yahoo Finance copy; the original reuters.com link is not named there. Figures are intraday-to-close as printed by Reuters (BigGo gives the final Nasdaq close as -2.14%).
